map.查「乾卦」六爻爻辞梗概: Overview of the Qian hexagram's six line statements
map.：乾卦六爻皆阳，爻题初九至上九：初九“潜龙勿用”、九二“见龙在田”、九三“君子终: : all six lines of Qian are yang, titled Chujiu to Shangjiu: Chujiu 'hidden dragon, do not act', Jiuer 'dragon appears in the field', Jiusan 'gentleman works all day', Jiusi 'perhaps leaps in the abyss', Jiuwu 'flying dragon in the sky', Shangjiu 'arrogant dragon, regret'; plus 'using nine, dragons without a head, auspicious'. The six lines show yang rising from hidden to extreme then 'fullness cannot last'—a textbook case of Zhouyi line-position thought.

map.爻题里的“初九”“六三”怎么读？: How to read line titles like 'Chujiu' and 'Liusan'?
map.爻题由“爻位+爻性”组成：初/二/三/四/五/上表从下往上的爻位，九=阳爻、六=: A line title combines 'position + polarity': Chu/Er/San/Si/Wu/Shang mark the position from bottom up; Jiu = yang line, Liu = yin line. So 'Chujiu' = lowest yang line, 'Liusan' = third yin line, 'Shangliu' = top yin line. To find a statement, first fix the hexagram, then the moving-line position.
map.为什么阳爻称“九”、阴爻称“六”？: Why are yang lines called 'nine' and yin lines 'six'?
map.源于《周易》用“老阳九、老阴六”标记阴阳（与筮法过揲之数相关：老阳策数 36÷4: From the Zhouyi marking yin/yang as 'old yang nine, old yin six' (tied to the yarrow-stalk counts: old yang 36÷4=9, old yin 24÷4=6). Later 'nine' stood for yang lines and 'six' for yin lines in titles, matching the line glyphs (— / --).
